guidelines.detail: same as LRN-006 (The description requires both activities without specifying their order, and the records identify the missing split and join gateways. This is already captured by learned guideline LRN-006.)

same as LRN-070 (The description distinguishes the repair actions and the subsequent functionality test, while the generated labels combine actions or omit described distinctions. This supports preserving the described actions in task labels. LRN-070 already says to preserve the described action, object, scope, and direction in labels, so this guideline is essentially the same.)

same as LRN-070 (The label pairs show actions being combined or added, and the descriptions distinguish the activities and their scope. LRN-070 already says to preserve the described action and object in the corresponding element label without replacing them with related actions or adding unsupported details.)

documentation rule FLOW-01 not applied (The reference includes a start-event-to-initial-activity flow that is absent from the generated model (F12). FLOW-01 already instructs using sequence flows to represent execution order between flow nodes, which covers this connection.)

same as LRN-070 (The label pairs show divergence in how activities are described, and the process description distinguishes the repair activities from the subsequent functionality test. LRN-070 already states this labeling principle.)

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description states that the process ends under one condition but, under another, continues with additional or recurring work.: Model the continuing alternative as a branch connected to the existing process flow, rather than as a detached start-to-end chain.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description states that a condition after an activity determines whether the process continues with further or recurring work or ends.

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description names multiple required activities without specifying their order and states that a later outcome depends on all of them: Model the activities as parallel branches and synchronize them before that outcome.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description states that multiple required activities may be performed in any order and that a later step depends on completion of all of them

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description states an activity, its object, scope, or recipient: Label the corresponding BPMN element so that it preserves the described action, object, scope, and direction; do not replace them with a related action or add unsupported details.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description identifies distinct actions within an activity or specifies an activity’s object or scope

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description says that a result determines whether the process finishes or performs another activity selected from alternatives: Model the result as an exclusive choice, route execution only through the selected alternative or to completion, and do not use a parallel join that waits for tokens from mutually exclusive paths. Represent any required repetition explicitly.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description says that a result determines whether the process finishes or performs another activity selected from alternatives

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description identifies a concrete action that initiates the process: Model that action as an activity after the start event, and connect it by sequence flow to the next described activity.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description identifies an initiating action followed by a process activity

rules_sent_back.instruction: Use bpmn:sequenceFlow for execution order between flow nodes in the same process or subprocess scope; set valid sourceRef and targetRef values.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description identifies an activity that begins the process after its stated trigger
